title_ne: अर्थ सम्बन्धी केही नेपाल कानूनलाई संशोधन र खारेज गर्ने विधेयक, २०८३
summary:
The name of this bill is "Some Nepal Acts Relating to Finance Amendment and Repeal Act, 2083" (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). The main purpose of this bill is to repeal legal and institutional provisions that are not in line with the spirit and sentiment of the Constitution of Nepal and appear irrelevant in the context of the present federal governance structure, end legal duplication, and ensure effective public service delivery at lower time and cost (Explanatory Note, Page 1). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

This provision covers any person or entity transporting goods for commercial purposes using a legally registered transport vehicle, which includes mechanically powered passenger vehicles, lorries, trucks, mini-trucks, containers, bullets, tankers, pickups, vans, and tractors used for transporting goods (Section 2, Subsection 1, Page 1-2). When transporting goods for commercial purposes using such transport vehicles, the details must be entered into a web-based online transport vehicle monitoring system before transporting (Section 2, Subsection 1, Page 1). Users of transport vehicles must keep a printed copy of the goods declaration and documents specified by the Department with them during the transport period (Section 2, Subsection 2, Page 2). Owners of transport vehicles registered or to be registered in Nepal must register the serial number of a working GPS device showing geo-location according to standards fixed by the Department and install it on their transport vehicle, though the Department may specify that certain transport vehicles or vehicles running in certain locations do not need such device installed (Section 2, Subsection 3 and 4, Page 2). The deadline for transport vehicle users to keep documents with them is during the transport period (Section 2, Subsection 2, Page 2). Deadlines for other tasks are not stated in the bill (Section 2, Subsection 1 and 3, Page 1-2).

Standards specified by the Department shall apply to working GPS devices showing geo-location (Section 2, Subsection 3, Page 2). For re-inspection of goods cleared by the customs office, the Department or a subordinate officer may take such goods into control to conduct re-inspection or necessary investigation and action (Section 4, Subsection 1, Page 5). Provisions are made for post-clearance testing and necessary checking, investigation, and action to control smuggling of goods from inside or outside customs areas (Section 4, Subsection 2 and 3, Page 5). Licensing and certification provisions are not stated in the bill.

For failing to enter details in the online monitoring system, failing to keep a printed copy of the declaration and documents during transport, or failing to install a registered GPS device, the Tax Officer may fine the concerned transport vehicle owner or user up to Rs. 50 thousand for the first time, and up to Rs. 1 lakh each time thereafter (Section 2, Subsection 6, Page 3). If additional non-tax liability is determined upon investigation for non-payment of non-tax payable under prevailing law, a fine of 100 percent of such additional non-tax amount shall be recovered (Section 3, Subsection 2, Page 4). The Tax Officer imposes fines for transport-related offences (Section 2, Subsection 6, Page 3), while fines determined after investigation of non-tax liability are recovered (Section 3, Subsection 2, Page 4). A right exists to apply for administrative review against decisions made by the Director General regarding non-tax assessment (Section 3, Subsection 3, Page 5). The time limit and court for review or appeal are not stated in the bill (Section 3, Subsection 3, Page 5).

This bill repeals the Provincial Development Plans (Implementation) Act, 2013, Increasing Circulation of Nepali Currency Act, 2014, Income Stamp Duty Act, 2019, Revenue Leakage (Investigation and Control) Act, 2052, Financial Intermediary Institutions Act, 2055, and Revenue Leakage (Investigation and Control) Rules, 2070 (Section 5, Subsection 1, Page 5-6). Complaints registered with the Revenue Investigation Department at the commencement of this Act that are under investigation or where investigation is complete but cases are yet to be filed shall be transferred as follows: income tax, excise duty, value added tax, and non-tax matters to the Inland Revenue Department; smuggling export or import matters to the Customs Department; and foreign exchange offences to the investigation officer designated under Section 11A of the Foreign Exchange (Regulation) Act, 2019 (Section 5, Subsection 2, Page 6). Records in the Revenue Investigation Department shall be managed to transfer to the respective bodies as per the decision of the Government of Nepal, Ministry of Finance (Section 5, Subsection 3, Page 6). What happens to the staff, assets, and funds of the repealed or replaced bodies is not stated in the bill (Section 5, Subsection 1, 2 and 3, Page 5-6).
